scope: JSDOM interaction and catalogue model checks; no browser layout or performance assertion

checks.label: New published pet receives its own stable detail URL and catalogue metadata
Six species stats are read back without changing the seeded data
Unpublished pet submissions do not appear in the catalogue
Renaming a local pet preserves identity and updates its stats
A deletion proposal leaves the published pet available until reviewed
Reviewed deletion retains a tombstone with its reason and redirection
A new submission cannot overwrite an existing pet by reusing its slug
Unknown species data does not become zero-filled radar values
A published advanced branch survives nested and range data unchanged
Historical display overrides cannot mask published skill changes
Pet catalogue offers add-pet but no broad directory edit
Pet cards and filter headings do not acquire injected edit buttons
Skill overview retains description and effect filters without row editors
Pet skill pool navigates to skill detail with the originating pet preserved
Original Counter records explicitly show both bloodlines as unrecorded
Pet maintenance offers an explicit deletion proposal rather than immediate deletion
New and renamed pets appear immediately in the catalogue
A local pet opens its own detail page, with the published name and species data
Local detail editors preserve the stable identity and return URL
A newly published pet can enter the same comparison tool
Reviewed deleted pets leave the catalogue
Old local references show the reviewed tombstone without destroying related records
Public skill detail displays disjoint ranges and a nested any-condition group
Public skill detail displays child branches and otherwise results
Skill detail retains a focused entry editor and each branch editor
Unknown bloodline and confirmed no-bloodline are distinct claims
Changing either side's bloodline creates a separate support pool
Dormant names under an unknown status do not create false equipped-bloodline claims
A vote on unknown configurations is not counted for a specified configuration
Published record projection preserves each side's selected or absent bloodline
Changing only bloodlines revises the published Counter claim
Public Counter reader shows the two published configurations with their notes
Renaming a pet preserves its earlier published Counter records under the stable identity
Visitor voting records support for the currently visible claim
Rerendering a new bloodline configuration clears the previous vote state and announcement
Automatic heading edits reject catalogue, filter and account screens
Unmarked custom headings are not assumed to be editable documents
Known knowledge articles and explicit article sections remain editable
Real article headings receive one contextual edit while UI notices receive none
Article heading edit preserves current query and stable anchor
No native select or React DOM errors were introduced by these flows
